title: 1.2.25 typeof Round-Up
description: Run typeof over six different values and find the one answer that lies. Auto-graded.

steps.title: A string and a number
steps.instructions: Log the type of a piece of text and the type of a number.

steps.title: A boolean and an undefined
steps.instructions: Log the type of true, and the type of undefined.

steps.title: null
steps.instructions: Log the type of null. Watch the answer: it is the one that lies.

steps.title: An object
steps.instructions: Log the type of an object written with curly braces, such as { name: "Sarah" }.

requirements.title: typeof a string
requirements.description: Logs the type of a quoted piece of text, either inline or via a variable holding one. Help: 1.2.23 (The typeof Operator)
requirements.hint: No line logs the type of quoted text yet. Put the quotes straight inside typeof, or use the name of a variable you set to a string.

requirements.title: typeof a number
requirements.description: Logs the type of a plain number, either inline or via a variable holding one. Help: 1.2.23 (The typeof Operator)
requirements.hint: No line logs the type of a number yet. Put the number straight inside typeof, or use the name of a variable you set to one.

requirements.title: typeof true
requirements.description: Logs the type of a boolean, either inline or via a variable holding true/false. Help: 1.2.23 (The typeof Operator)
requirements.hint: No line logs the type of true yet. Put true straight inside typeof, or use the name of a variable you set to true or false.

requirements.title: typeof undefined
requirements.description: Logs the type of undefined, either inline or via a variable left unassigned. Help: 1.2.20 (The undefined Value)
requirements.hint: No line logs the type of undefined yet. Put undefined straight inside typeof, or use the name of a variable you declared with let and never gave a value.

requirements.title: typeof null
requirements.description: Logs the type of null: the answer that is a known bug: either inline or via a variable holding null. Help: 1.2.19 (The null Value)
requirements.hint: No line logs the type of null yet. Put null straight inside typeof, or use the name of a variable you set to null.

requirements.title: typeof an object
requirements.description: Logs the type of an object written with curly braces, either inline or via a variable holding one. Help: 1.2.23 (The typeof Operator)
requirements.hint: No line logs the type of an object yet. If a variable holds your object, log typeof followed by that variable's own name -- not the name of a property inside it.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "1.2.25 typeof Round-Up". The task they were given: Log the type of a piece of text and the type of a number. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
